entries.title: Judges 9:1
segments: Shechem; a city in the tribe of Ephraim, lying between mount Gerizim on the south, and mount Ebal on the north.

entries.title: Judges 9:2
segments: Your bone; a Shechemite and a relative.
Men who earnestly desire power, and flatter their fellow men to obtain it, are not worthy to be trusted, and should not be chosen to rule over others.

entries.title: Judges 9:3
segments: Men are easily flattered, and their judgment, feelings, and conduct often biassed towards those who are related to or connected with them.

entries.title: Judges 9:4
segments:
House of Baal-berith; the place of their idol-worship. 
 
Vain and light persons, the vicious and the worthless of all descriptions, will prostitute their political influence to the support of those flatterers who like themselves are vicious, and who will furnish them with money.

entries.title: Judges 9:5
segments: Ambitious men, who are given up of God to the gratification of their lusts, will commit any crime to secure their selfish objects.

entries.title: Judges 9:6
segments: House of Millo; a tower or castle in the city.  It seems to have been the same as "the tower of Sechem,"

.  The men of Shechem and the house of Millo are separately mentioned in Jotham's curse, and, in like manner, the destruction of the men of Shechem and the men of the tower of Shechem is separately recorded. 
 
When a people choose immoral men as their rulers, they will generally be made instruments of mutual punishment to each other.

entries.title: Judges 9:7
segments: Gerizim; a mountain on the south side of Shechem.

entries.title: Judges 9:8
segments:
The trees went forth; this is the commencement of a parable, representing the folly of the Shechemites in making Abimelech king. 
 
Parables may be a most effective and useful method of inculcating divine truth, and he who wisely employs them be an eminent benefactor of mankind.

entries.title: Judges 9:9
segments:
Olive-tree; a tree yielding oil, used not only in food, but also in the worship of God and in the consecration of men to public office. 
 
Wise men will not be anxious to leave the safe, quiet, and useful pursuits and enjoyments of private life, for the sake of becoming rulers, especially over the wicked.

entries.title: Judges 9:13
segments: Wine, which cheereth God; it was employed in his worship, and thus pleased him.

entries.title: Judges 9:14
segments: The bramble; one of the meanest and most worthless shrubs.  Gideon, who like the olive, fig-tree, and vine, was useful, refused; but Abimelech, who like the bramble was worthless, consented to be made king.

entries.title: Judges 9:15
segments:
Let fire come out; this expressed the trouble which Abimelech would bring upon the chief men of Shechem, represented as cedars. 
 
Those who are most unfaithful and worthless in private life, are often most anxious for promotion to public life; and those who thus promote them, may expect through them to reap the fruit of their folly.

entries.title: Judges 9:16
segments: Truly; rightly, in a proper manner.

entries.title: Judges 9:19
segments: Teachers of divine truth in all ages have maintained that godliness is profitable unto all things, and that the way of transgressors is hard; that righteousness tendeth to life; and that those who continue in wickedness do it to their own death.

entries.title: Judges 9:20
segments: Let fire come out; fire will come out; expressive of the mutual calamities which Abimelech and the men of Shechem would bring on each other.

entries.title: Judges 9:21
segments: Beer; a place south of Shechem.

entries.title: Judges 9:23
segments:
God sent; suffered, through the temptation of Satan to arise in their own hearts. 
 
The wicked have no permanent bond of union, safety, or peace; and those who have been treacherous and cruel to others, will ordinarily meet with others who will be treacherous and cruel to them.

entries.title: Judges 9:25
segments: Liers in wait; to kill Abimelech, who was then absent from the city, or to take him prisoner on his return.

entries.title: Judges 9:26
segments: Gaal; supposed to be a Canaanite, pretending to have descended from Hamor the father of Shechem, and former prince of that country.
Men may rebel against one set of wicked rulers, and yet choose another who are no better; and, by so doing, may only increase their distress and hasten their ruin.

entries.title: Judges 9:27
segments: Their god; their idol-god.
Dissipation, rioting, and licentiousness are not true liberty, and those who indulge in them can never enjoy it.

entries.title: Judges 9:28
segments:
Who is Abimelech; that he should reign over the ancient and renowned city of Shechem. 
 
  Zebul; the governor of Shechem during Abimelech's absence.
Boasting, pride, and self-esteem are forerunners of defeat, degradation, and contempt.

entries.title: Judges 9:29
segments:
Said to Abimelech; that is, by messengers, for Abimelech himself was absent from the city. 
 
  Increase--come out; a challenge to Abimelech to make his army as strong as possible, and meet him on the field of battle.

entries.title: Judges 9:31
segments: Sent messengers--privily; because he was not strong enough to offer direct resistance to Gaal, who had won over the people of the city to his side.

entries.title: Judges 9:37
segments: Middle of the land; rather, height of the land; that is, from the high hills bordering Shechem.  See note to

. 
 
  The plain of Meonenim; rather, the oak of Meonenim; that is, in English, the enchanters' oak.

entries.title: Judges 9:38
segments: Those who pretend to despise their enemies when at a distance, are often afraid of them when they come near; and the most reproachful in time of safety, are often most cowardly in time of danger.

entries.title: Judges 9:41
segments: Arumah; a place near Shechem.

entries.title: Judges 9:43
segments:
He; Abimelech. 
 
  Took; had taken.

entries.title: Judges 9:45
segments:
Sowed it with salt; in token of its desolation. 
 
The men who aid and exalt the wicked, are often the men who are injured and destroyed by them.

entries.title: Judges 9:46
segments: The courses which wicked men take to secure their safety not unfrequently accelerate their ruin; and often by those whom they have aided in slaying others, they are themselves slain.

entries.title: Judges 9:48
segments: Zalmon; meaning shady; supposed to be so called from its being covered with forests.

entries.title: Judges 9:50
segments: Thebez; a city of Ehpraim, a few miles north-east of Shechem.

entries.title: Judges 9:51
segments: A strong tower; such towers in or near cities, to which the people fled in time of danger, were common.

entries.title: Judges 9:52
segments: Success often renders men reckless, and when they are most confident they are nearest to destruction.  They may escape the greatest apparent dangers, and then fall by such as are not thought of.

entries.title: Judges 9:53
segments: A millstone; the upper stone of a hand-mill, in which the women ground their grain.
All-to; an old English term meaning, wholly, entirely.

entries.title: Judges 9:54
segments:
A woman slew him; to be slain by a woman was considered disgraceful. 
 
Men, especially warriors, think much about an honorable death and sometimes are peculiarly sensitive of their reputation when sinking into shame and everlasting contempt.

entries.title: Judges 9:56
segments: Rendered; requited or punished.
Jehovah is a God that judgeth in the earth, and often here proclaims the sins of men in their punishment.

entries.title: Judges 9:57
segments: The curse of Jotham;
